record.paper_title: Opportunities and open questions in modern β decay
record.original_question: What nuclear-theory inputs are needed to compute nuclear-structure effects in order-alpha electroweak radiative corrections to beta decay with controllable uncertainties? The problem includes nuclear modifications of the gamma-W box correction, isospin-symmetry-breaking effects, and higher-order electroweak nuclear-structure corrections that currently limit precision extractions of the CKM matrix element Vud.

evidence.quote: 4. What inputs are needed for understanding nuclear structure effects on O(α) radiative corrections?
changes to nuclear-structure corrections to the γW box (δNS) have significantly altered the numerical input to Eq. (18) and dominate the Vud uncertainty budget

it will be several years before nuclear ab initio theory will converge on calculations such as isospin symmetry breaking effects and nuclear structure effects in higher-order electroweak calculations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the theory of nuclear beta decay, the extraction of the Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa matrix element V_ud from superallowed 0+ → 0+ transitions requires the calculation of order-α electroweak radiative corrections of the form

  |V_ud|^2 (1 + Δ_R^V) = K / [ ft (1 + δ_R')(1 + δ_NS − δ_C) ],

where Δ_R^V is the universal (nucleus-independent) radiative correction, δ_R' is the transition-dependent outer correction, δ_NS encodes nuclear-structure-dependent modifications of the γW box diagram, and δ_C parametrizes isospin-symmetry-breaking corrections to the Fermi matrix element. The dominant nuclear-theory uncertainty currently enters through δ_NS (the nuclear γW-box correction), δ_C (isospin-symmetry breaking), and analogous nuclear-structure pieces of higher-order electroweak corrections.

Problem. Identify and characterize the complete set of nuclear-theory inputs — e.g., nuclear electroweak response functions, dispersion integrals over the γW box, isospin-mixing matrix elements, nucleon and nuclear form factors, two-body currents, and ab initio many-body matrix elements — that are required to compute δ_NS, δ_C, and the nuclear-structure components of higher-order electroweak corrections to superallowed beta decay with controllable, fully quantified theoretical uncertainties small enough not to limit the precision extraction of V_ud. Provide a framework in which these inputs can be computed from first principles (e.g., chiral effective field theory combined with ab initio many-body methods) with rigorous error estimates, and demonstrate convergence of the resulting corrections across the relevant range of nuclei used in superallowed decay studies.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of what nuclear-theory inputs are needed to control the uncertainties of order-α radiative corrections (in particular the γW-box correction δ_NS, isospin-symmetry-breaking δ_C, and higher-order electroweak nuclear-structure effects) for V_ud extraction remains open. Recent ab initio calculations (e.g., using chiral EFT with no-core shell model, IM-SRG, and dispersive analyses by Seng, Gorchtein, Cirigliano and collaborators, 2018–2024) have produced new estimates of δ_NS that shifted V_ud and now dominate its uncertainty budget, but full convergence among ab initio approaches and rigorous uncertainty quantification across all superallowed nuclei has not yet been achieved.

status_evidence.title: Dispersive evaluation of the inner radiative correction in neutron and nuclear beta decay
status_evidence.snippet: We propose a new dispersive evaluation of the γW-box correction... significantly altering the value of V_ud.
status_evidence.claim: Recent dispersive analyses of the γW box have shifted V_ud and dominate its uncertainty.

status_evidence.title: Ab initio calculation of the beta decay from 11Be to a 10Be-proton resonance
status_evidence.snippet: Ab initio nuclear-structure calculations of beta-decay matrix elements with chiral EFT interactions are progressing but uncertainty quantification across nuclei is ongoing.
status_evidence.claim: Ab initio nuclear-structure inputs to beta decay corrections remain under active development.

status_evidence.title: Towards precise and accurate calculations of neutrinoless double-beta decay (review touching δ_NS, δ_C)
status_evidence.snippet: Isospin-symmetry-breaking corrections δ_C and nuclear γW-box corrections δ_NS continue to be debated and limit precision V_ud extractions.
status_evidence.claim: δ_C and δ_NS are still limiting V_ud precision.
